clue.text: Whip round?

definitions.meaning: to whip is to thrash or flog someone

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: thrash somebody, or the route a constable walks on patrol.

clue.text: Second piece of pork? It's game!

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it, i.e. to back it
gammon is cured ham from the hind leg of a pig

explanation.surface: A diner reaching for a second helping of pork declares it fine fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal but is the verb meaning support. GAMMON is a cut of bacon-cured pork, familiar on British menus.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a two-player board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Protective covering for part of the stage

definitions.meaning: a garment tied over clothes while cooking
the section of a theatre stage in front of the curtain

explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen garment shields clothes, and in theatres the forestage before the proscenium carries the same name.

clue.text: Go out with girl on the river

parts.note: Sally is a girl's name
the Forth is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A young man heads off on a date with a girl, boating on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out boldly, as soldiers once made a sortie from a besieged fort.

clue.text: Fines could be devised to scare me

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so the letters may be put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a schedule of penalties might be designed to frighten them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be devised' rearranges SCAREME; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To amerce is an old legal verb meaning to punish with a monetary penalty, so this is a verb sense.

clue.text: Drawn hyperbolically?

parts.note: an archer's weapon pulled back, and also the idiom 'draw the ...', meaning to tell exaggerated tales

explanation.surface: A picture sketched with wild exaggeration.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'draw the long bow' is an old idiom for telling tall stories; 'hyperbolically' points to that idiom while 'Drawn' suggests a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the bow an archer draws, and drawing it is the idiom for overstating things.

clue.text: Not strong enough to hold the basket

definitions.meaning: a rush basket for packing figs or raisins

explanation.surface: Someone is too weak to carry the basket.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is feeble or delicate; the other is an old word for a rush container used for dried fruit.

clue.text: Mournful river bird — not yet replete

parts.note: an egret is a white heron

indicators.note: something not yet complete stops short, so the final letter of the word is missing

parts.note: replete means full

explanation.surface: A sad wading bird by the river still has not had its fill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not yet replete' is FULL one letter short: FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorrow over what has passed; full of sadness.

clue.text: Isn't the sole occupant of the elevator

indicators.note: occupant of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is not alone riding in the lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isn't the sole' is a playful definition: the back of a shoe is next to, but not, its underside.
explanation.definitionFit: On a shoe this part is the raised back, distinct from the flat underside.

clue.text: Grey-coat school to fall into this class?

indicators.note: to school letters is to drill them into line, falling into a new order

explanation.surface: Pupils of a grey-uniformed school are sorted into a form group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school to fall into' rearranges GREYCOAT; 'this' is only a link, and Grey Coat is also a real London school name.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of things sharing some characteristic, a division in a classification.

clue.text: Scrap material brought in to cleanse boat bottom of seaweed

indicators.note: one piece is brought in to sit inside the other

parts.note: to careen a ship is to tilt it on its side to clean or repair its hull
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone uses an old cloth to scrub weed off a hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap material' reads as rubbish fabric but supplies the inserted piece; careening is the old shipwright's practice of beaching a vessel on its side, and 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish moss, a red alga gathered from Atlantic shores and used to make a gelling agent.

clue.text: Fish's head coming out from the seaweed

indicators.note: the head of the word is removed, so its opening letter leaves

parts.note: tangle is a large brown seaweed, a kind of kelp

explanation.surface: A fish pokes its head out of the weed.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to try to catch with rod and line.

clue.text: Low down? That's due to bottled spirit

parts.note: the low-down is inside information, which is also called gen in British slang
i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Someone feeling glum blames it on drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low down' looks like a mood but is the noun for inside info; 'due to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale a jinni is shut in a lamp or flask until released.

clue.text: Intrigued, sailor rang around

indicators.note: the word for rang goes around the sailor, enclosing it

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone or call them
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: Curious, a seaman phoned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To form a secret faction is to conspire or plot, which is this sense of intrigued.

clue.text: Fish hard to get, on the river-—- but novel outcome

parts.note: the bleak is a small European river fish
H stands for hard, as on pencils
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: An angler finds the fish elusive but makes a good story of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' and 'novel' both look like adjectives; 'to get, on' and 'but' are links. The OUSE is a river in Yorkshire and another in East Anglia.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dickens's long book about the Jarndyce lawsuit.

clue.text: Birds in a flurry in the countryside

indicators.note: the birds are set in, around, the commotion

parts.note: mews are gulls
an ado is a fuss or flurry

explanation.surface: Birds take off in a panic over the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Birds in a flurry' paints panicking flocks, but 'in' is the container signal; mews as gulls is an old word solvers meet often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland fields of open farmland, a typical rural scene.

clue.text: Aghast when weak crust collapses

indicators.note: a crust that collapses falls apart, so its letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A baker is horrified when a pie top caves in.
explanation.definitionFit: Filled with awe or dismay, struck dumb with shock.

clue.text: Forlorn little women sit out flu, in sorry state

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women

indicators.note: out means put out of place, so these letters shift
a word in a sorry state is in disarray, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Wretched little women sit out an illness in a pitiable way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little women' calls up Alcott's novel but is just the abbreviation; 'out' scrambles the first short word (giving IST) and 'in sorry state' the second (giving FUL).
explanation.definitionFit: Yearning, sadly longing for something lost.

clue.text: Second printing may incite public disorder

parts.note: an edition is one print run of a book

explanation.surface: A reissued pamphlet could stir up unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may incite' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech or action stirring rebellion against the state, a cause of civil unrest.

clue.text: Like pins and needles? Only needles

definitions.text: Like pins and needles? Only needles

parts.words: Like pins and needles? Only needles
parts.note: a sewing needle has a single hole for the thread, while a pin has none

explanation.surface: A question about the tingling sensation in a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pins and needles' suggests the tingling feeling; really it is about the hole a sewing needle has.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a single eye, as every sewing needle does.

clue.text: Plain speaking when police backed into riot

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

indicators.note: a riot throws the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Frank talk as officers retreat into a street riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is fodder, not a link: 'riot' scrambles it to TION; 'backed' turns CID into DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear enunciation, the manner of pronouncing words.

clue.text: Character finding, with a throw of the dice, all is lost

indicators.note: a throw of the dice scatters them, so the letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler finds that one roll of the dice loses everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a throw of' mixes DICE and ALL; 'the' and 'is lost' are surface padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A cedilla is a typographic mark, a written sign placed under c in French.

clue.text: Turtle meat with cold beer, having eaten nutty pie

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the beer has eaten the other piece, so it now sits inside

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so the letters go haywire

explanation.surface: A diner pairs turtle meat with cold beer after a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nutty' sounds like a flavour of the pie but makes IPE from it; 'having eaten' puts that inside the beer. Calipee was prized in Victorian turtle soup.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellowish edible part next to the lower shell of a turtle, used in soup.

clue.text: The Inca ladies initially cooked Edith this mix

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'The Inca ladies initially cooked Edith this mix (8)': THE INCA + L anagram gives the letters, but 'Edith this mix' looks like an OCR garble and no definition can be identified.
annotationWithheld.clue: The Inca ladies initially cooked Edith this mix

clue.text: Prophet of human disaster

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks the order of things, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A seer foretells catastrophe for mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the twelve minor Old Testament seers, who foretold the fall of Nineveh.

clue.text: Light burden for one with a cause

definitions.meaning: a portable lamp or flaming brand

definitions.text: burden for one with a cause
definitions.meaning: someone devoted to a cause is said to carry this for it

explanation.definitionFit: It is a flashlight or flaming brand, and the thing a devotee 'carries' for a cause or a beloved.

clue.text: It's about to fold, but can be making a come-back

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to ply is an old word for to fold or bend

explanation.surface: A folding chair that keeps springing back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'but can be making a' are links; 'come-back' means a retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort or answer in return.

clue.text: A stone circle seen with a friend

parts.note: O is circle-shaped
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend visits a prehistoric stone ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A gemstone with iridescent play of colour.

clue.text: Parking in abundance-but costly

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
lush means growing thickly, luxuriant

explanation.surface: Ample parking, though it costs a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxurious and expensive-looking.

clue.text: Two politicians I rout in offhand way

definitions.text: Two politicians I rout in offhand way

indicators.note: done in a careless, offhand way, so the letters fall into a casual new order

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, so two of them gives MP twice

explanation.surface: A candidate boasts of beating two parliamentarians off the cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: Two MPs plus I and ROUT are shuffled; read whole, the clue describes an unrehearsed victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Done without preparation, off the cuff.

clue.text: Denied milk could be agreeing with one

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be arranged as something else

explanation.surface: A child refused milk could still be on someone's side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing the same opinions as another person.

clue.text: Narrow strait running through rocky ledges

indicators.note: the answer runs through the words, hidden across the join

explanation.surface: A slim channel flows between rocky shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: KYLE is a Scottish word for a narrow sea channel, as in the Kyle of Lochalsh.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland it names a sound or channel between islands or an island and mainland.
